title: “Monks, those ascetics or brahmins who are tied, infatuated, utterly committed to these five strands of sensual pleasure, who do not see their peril, who…
content: “Monks, those ascetics or brahmins who are tied, infatuated, utterly committed to these five strands of sensual pleasure, who do not see their peril, who do not know the escape from them, and who enjoy them—they should be understood as having fallen into misfortune, into calamity, and are being used by Māra as he wishes. Monks, just as a forest deer that has fallen into a trap must lie down—that deer should be understood as having fallen into misfortune, into calamity, and is being used by the hunter as he wishes. When the hunter comes, the deer cannot leave as it wishes. So too, monks, those ascetics or brahmins who are tied … are being used by Māra as he wishes.”

title: “Householder, suppose there is a hungry, weak dog at a slaughterhouse. A skilled butcher or his apprentice throws it a bone that has been well-scraped,…
content: “Householder, suppose there is a hungry, weak dog at a slaughterhouse. A skilled butcher or his apprentice throws it a bone that has been well-scraped, thoroughly scraped, with no meat left, only smeared with blood. What do you think, householder? Would that dog, by gnawing on that bone — well-scraped, thoroughly scraped, with no meat, only smeared with blood — be able to dispel its hunger and weakness?” “No, venerable sir. Why is that? Because that bone is well-scraped, thoroughly scraped, with no meat, only smeared with blood; the dog would only get weary and distressed.” “So too, householder, a noble disciple reflects: ‘The Blessed One has said that sensual pleasures are like a bone — of much suffering, much despair, and the peril is even greater.’ Having seen this as it actually is with perfect wisdom, having abandoned the equanimity based on diversity, dependent on diversity, and having cultivated the equanimity based on unity, dependent on unity, where all clinging to the world’s materials is completely abandoned without remainder, he cultivates such equanimity.”

title: “Monks, here a clansman, abandoning sensual pleasures, goes forth from the household life into homelessness. But because of those sensual pleasures, or other sensual pleasures…
content: “Monks, here a clansman, abandoning sensual pleasures, goes forth from the household life into homelessness. But because of those sensual pleasures, or other sensual pleasures worse than those, he is destroyed, ruined, falls, lies prostrate. These five hindrances, monks, are obscurations, hindrances, coverings of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. What five? Sensual desire, monks, is an obscuration, a hindrance, a covering of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. Ill-will … sloth and torpor … restlessness and remorse … doubt, monks, is an obscuration, a hindrance, a covering of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. These five hindrances, monks, are obscurations, hindrances, coverings of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. The seven factors of enlightenment, monks, are not obscurations, not hindrances, not coverings of the mind; when developed and cultivated, they lead to the realization of the fruit of true knowledge and liberation. What seven? The mindfulness factor of enlightenment … The equanimity factor of enlightenment — these are not obscurations, not hindrances, not coverings of the mind; when developed and cultivated, they lead to the realization of the fruit of true knowledge and liberation.”

title: “‘The world is deficient, longing, a slave to craving’ — that, great king, is the fourth exposition of the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One,…
content: “‘The world is deficient, longing, a slave to craving’ — that, great king, is the fourth exposition of the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Having known, seen, and heard that exposition, I went forth from the household life into homelessness.”

title: “Monks, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, thought: ‘This Dhamma that I have realized is deep, hard to see, hard to…
content: “Monks, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, thought: ‘This Dhamma that I have realized is deep, hard to see, hard to awaken to, peaceful, sublime, beyond the sphere of logic, subtle, to be understood by the wise. But this generation delights in sensual pleasures, is devoted to sensual pleasures, is fond of sensual pleasures. For a generation that delights in sensual pleasures, is devoted to sensual pleasures, is fond of sensual pleasures, it is hard to see this principle of specific conditionality (dependent origination); it is hard to see the principle that all formations are peaceful, that all substrates of rebirth are eliminated, that craving is destroyed, that there is dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.’”

title: “I do not see any other form, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a man as the form of a woman. The…
content: “I do not see any other form, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a man as the form of a woman. The form of a woman, monks, obsesses and occupies the mind of a man.”

title: Elder Parāpariya: “Having abandoned the six sense-bases, With sense-doors well restrained, Having pulled out the root of evil, I have attained the destruction of defilements.”
content:
Elder Parāpariya:
“Having abandoned the six sense-bases,
With sense-doors well restrained,
Having pulled out the root of evil,
I have attained the destruction of defilements.”

title: Elder Tissa: “As if struck by a sword, As if his head were on fire, Mindful, a monk should go forth, Abandoning sensual lust.”
content:
Elder Tissa:
“As if struck by a sword,
As if his head were on fire,
Mindful, a monk should go forth,
Abandoning sensual lust.”

title: “Monks, the large deep lake refers to sensual pleasures. Monks, the great herd of deer refers to beings. Monks, the man who does not desire…
content: “Monks, the large deep lake refers to sensual pleasures. Monks, the great herd of deer refers to beings. Monks, the man who does not desire their welfare, benefit, security refers to Māra the Evil One. Monks, the dangerous path refers to the wrong eightfold path – wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration. Monks, the male decoy refers to delight and greed. Monks, the female decoy refers to ignorance. Monks, the man who desires their welfare, benefit, security refers to the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. The safe, secure path leading to happiness refers to the Noble Eightfold Path – right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.”

title: “So too, Māgandiya, contact with sensual pleasures in the past was painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the future will be…
content: “So too, Māgandiya, contact with sensual pleasures in the past was painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the future will be painful, very hot, very feverish; contact with sensual pleasures in the present is painful, very hot, very feverish. And these beings who have not abandoned lust for sensual pleasures, being consumed by craving for sensual pleasures, burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, with corrupt faculties, perceive as pleasure that which is actually painful contact with sensual pleasures.”
